slides.title: Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion distribution and steady-state convergence times in multi-agent networks, providing insights for the societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion consensus time in networks using a majority-based update rule.
card.key_idea: A 2k-choices rule is analyzed across three regimes (sub-critical, super-critical, critical) based on stubborn agent proportions, determining if convergence is exponential, logarithmic, or polynomial.
card.evaluation: Theoretically derived scaling laws for mixing times were numerically validated by solving forward Kolmogorov and detailed balance equations for various network sizes.
card.limitation: The analysis is conducted on a fully connected network, which may not generalize to all network topologies.

slides.title: HUI360: A 360° Egocentric Dataset and Baselines for Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation
slides.highlight: This work introduces HUI360, a large-scale 360° egocentric dataset and baselines for anticipating human intentions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HUI360 is the largest in-the-wild 360° egocentric dataset for anticipating human-robot physical interactions.
card.key_idea: An automated pipeline using YOLOv11x, SAM2.1-L, and ViTPose/Sapiens to detect, track, and annotate interactions based on segmentation mask intersections with robot zones.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using RF, MLP, and LSTM baselines on HUI360 and SSUP-A datasets via AUC, F1-score, and Average Precision across various forecasting horizons.
card.limitation: Only captures physical interactions (e.g., picking/placing), ignoring nuanced social signals like gaze, hesitation, or verbal engagement.

slides.title: ComBodied Agents: a New Paradigm of Human-Centric Agentic AI
slides.highlight: This work introduces ComBodied Agents to bridge the gap between digital and embodied agents by focusing on modeling and supporting human-state trajectories. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Combodied Agents shift AI focus from external task completion to supporting longitudinal human-state trajectories.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop framework integrating multimodal human-state perception, longitudinal memory, Personal World Models (PWMs), and agency-preserving intervention policies to enhance human capability and autonomy.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the text proposes scenario-centered evaluation, agency-preservation metrics, and benchmark requirements rather than reporting specific results.
card.limitation: Requires managing fragmented, noisy, and discontinuous personal data while avoiding user dependence, manipulation, or loss of epistemic agency.

slides.title: X2-Turn: Frame-Synchronous Dual-Head Modeling for Joint Streaming ASR and Turn State Prediction
slides.highlight: X2-Turn enables real-time distinction between user interruptions, backchannels, and utterance completions. This supports HyECHO's goals regarding addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: X2-Turn enables joint, frame-synchronous streaming ASR and turn state prediction using a dual-head architecture.
card.key_idea: Extends Voxtral Realtime with a parallel turn state head and ASR-anchored supervision to predict turn states and ASR tokens simultaneously at 80ms intervals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on bilingual EasyTurn test sets against cascaded and streaming baselines; results show a strong accuracy-latency trade-off and competitive ASR performance.
card.limitation: Joint training introduces some ASR performance degradation compared to ASR-only training (Stage 1 vs Stage 2).

slides.title: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
slides.highlight: This research examines how institutional rules and authority states influence the safety and collective behavior of multi-agent systems, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: AI safety depends on institutional design, specifically how rules are communicated and how authority is tracked.
card.key_idea: Comparing constitutional prompts, local-state guards, and provenance-aware guards to show that identical violation rates can mask different mechanisms of behavioral prevention versus mechanical containment.
card.evaluation: 5,280 episodes across four model families using structured delegation workflows and resource-allocation tasks; results show provenance guards prevent 'laundering' violations that local guards admit.
card.limitation: Uses synthetic, small-scale environments with limited action languages; results may not generalize to open-ended dialogue or complex real-world tool use.

slides.title: SAIN: Structure-Aware Interactive Navigation with Active Dialogue Grounding for Mobile Robot
slides.tldr: ZERO-SHOT INTERACTIVE NAVIGATION VIA DIALOGUE-TO-STATE CONVERSION
slides.highlight: SAIN introduces a framework that converts active dialogue into persistent structured memory to resolve ambiguous instructions during navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: SAIN converts active dialogue into persistent structured memories for zero-shot interactive instance goal navigation.
card.key_idea: A dialogue-to-state framework that compiles information, route, and disambiguation answers into target evidence, topological corridor masks, and object-candidate labels to guide long-horizon exploration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VL-LN IIGN benchmark; improved SR from 20.2 to 25.4 and SPL from 13.07 to 14.17 over the strongest dialogue-enabled baseline.

slides.title: DOBOT Unveils Humanoid Robot Designed for Life Beyond the Factory
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID ROBOT FOR NON-INDUSTRIAL USE
slides.highlight: The introduction of a humanoid robot designed for environments outside the factory is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing and transferring contact-rich human bathing demonstrations to a soft robotic hand, contributing to the development of safe physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a robot-assisted system.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as a processing primitive to reconstruct synchronized motion, shape, and force data, then retargets these to a soft robotic hand and arm.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world deployment on a mannequin using open- and closed-loop control.
card.limitation: Closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; lacks online human pose estimation for live human deployment.

slides.title: DOBOT Unveils All-Terrain Humanoid Robot LUMO
slides.tldr: ALL-TERRAIN HUMANOID ROBOT WITH VR TELEOPERATION
slides.highlight: The introduction of the LUMO all-terrain humanoid robot and its VR teleoperation capabilities is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.
